images.caption:
Dose rate meter, Pripjat, Ukraine
The normal environmental radiation in a non-contaminated area is 0.05 to 0.1 microsievert/h depending how high up you are. The geiger counter will give alarm at 0.3 microsievert/h as an unhealthy level, so 9 is pretty high. However, you would have to spend weeks in such a high level to acquire a dangerous dose for your body. 

There are also a lot of «hotspots» in the exclusion zone where you measure levels from 150 up to 800 microsievert/h. We measured 190 at some points, and mostly the levels changed rapidly in only a few steps... that's why we had a guide.
images.alt:
Dose rate meter, Pripjat, Ukraine

images.filename: Morphological anomaly of Scots Pine (Pinus sylvestris) near Pripyat.jpg
images.caption: A Scots Pine (Pinus sylvestris) exhibiting an atypical crown shape, photographed near the abandoned city of Pripyat (Chornobyl Exclusion Zone). The tree shows a loss of apical dominance, resulting in a multi-stemmed, bush-like structure. Such morphological anomalies are frequently observed in conifers within the Zone and can be attributed to the effects of ionizing radiation on meristematic tissues (buds) during growth, or potentially biotic stress factors.
images.alt: A Scots Pine (Pinus sylvestris) exhibiting an atypical crown shape, photographed near the abandoned city of Pripyat (Chornobyl Exclusion Zone). images.caption:
Security gates in a community centre in Chernobyl, Ukraine.
The gates have integrated Geiger-Müller tubes to detect radioactive contamination.

A person enters the gate sideways, placing hands on the detector panels for a few seconds. If no contamination is detected, the barrier opens and the person can step out the other side.
